hints.title: Biconnectivity and Bridge Discovery Obstacle
hints.text: A connection is critical if removing it disconnects the network, meaning it belongs to no cycle. How can recording entry timestamps and the lowest reachable discovery step in a recursive walk detect such bridge edges?

hints.title: Back-Edge Ancestor Reachability Invariant
hints.text: An edge (u, v) is a bridge if and only if no back-edge from the subtree of v can reach u or any ancestor of u.

hints.title: Tarjan Low-Link Bridge Detection Procedure
hints.text: Track discovery time and the lowest reachable time for every vertex during traversal. For each unvisited neighbor v of u, recurse on v and update the lowest reachable time of u with that of v. If the lowest reachable time of v remains strictly greater than the discovery time of u, then edge (u, v) has no alternative path back to u or its ancestors, so record it as a bridge.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Tarjan bridge algorithm visits every vertex and explores each undirected edge exactly twice.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating edge removal one by one takes O(E * (V + E)) which causes TLE for 10^5 edges.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency lists and timing arrays require O(V + E) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Implementing Tarjan low-link bridge finding algorithm in a single linear pass.
